title: Canary orchestra: roles, timeline and signal contracts (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience
This is a working draft to align product, SRE, serving runtime, and solutions engineering on a repeatable canary/A-B activation choreography. Goal: reduce cognitive load during activation, make signal contracts explicit, and provide a compact set of templates that teams can copy. Audience: product owners, release stewards, oncall SREs, solutions engineers, data scientists.

Quick summary (one-line)
A lightweight, role-first canary choreography that defines signal contracts, ramp timeline, and explicit decision gates so cross-functional teams can run low-friction, high-confidence micro-releases for LLM features.

Key principles
- Signals over anecdotes: prefer instrumented telemetry + blind test sets for quality.
- Fast, reversible exposure: small cohort -> automated checks -> graduated scale.
- Ownership clarity: one steward per canary, explicit escalation chain.
- Safety budget: explicit limits for latency, cost, and model quality that trigger automatic throttle/rollback.

Roles and responsibilities (compact)
- Release Steward (RS): coordinates stakeholders, owns hypothesis and activation plan. (Suggested: Product PM)
- Observability Lead (OL): author signal contract, ensures dashboards and alerts are ready. (SRE/Observability)
- Model Lead (ML): verifies model variant compatibility and quality baseline (Applied ML).
- Runtime Lead (RL): validates capacity and fallback policies (Serving/runtime infra).
- Solutions/CS liaison: customer-facing impact and comms if early adopters involved.
- Oncall responder: triages alerts during ramp windows.

Signal contract (must-have metrics)
1) Latency: p50, p95, p99 tail for target route. Thresholds: p95 increase <= +30% vs baseline OR absolute p95 > 1.2s => fail.
2) Errors: 5xx rate and API-level error responses (bad-request, model-failure). Threshold: 5xx > 0.5% absolute or x4 baseline.
3) Quality: combined automated rubric (synthetic prompts) + human review sample. Key quality metrics: hallucination rate, safe-inference rate, semantic-score (eval harness). Thresholds: regression > 2% absolute or delta worse than baseline > 5%.
4) Cost: per-request compute token estimate + net spend delta. Threshold: spend delta > 30% of expected monthly budget for the feature => throttle.
5) Business signals: user conversion funnels, retention signal delta monitoring (product metric owner).

How to author a signal contract (mini-template)
- Baseline window: 7–14 days of production traffic (or synthetic baseline if new route).
- Probe dataset: 200 canonical prompts representing edge and high-value slices (attach).
- Metric definitions: exact instrument names, query examples for dashboards, alert thresholds.
- Blind sample review process: 20 examples / day during ramp with reviewer roster.
- Escalation path: who to call at T+0, T+30m, T+2h.

Traffic ramp plan (example)
- Canary 0: 0.5% traffic for 30 minutes. Automated checks pass -> proceed.
- Canary 1: 2% traffic for 1 hour. Checks pass -> proceed.
- Canary 2: 10% traffic for 2 hours. Checks pass -> proceed.
- Gradual: 25% for 6 hours -> 50% for 24 hours -> full.
Notes: durations are customizable for latency-sensitive routes (shorter ramps) or critical flows (longer observation).

Automated gating rules (examples we should add to console)
- Abort if any hard threshold violated. Abort means: (a) route traffic back to last stable model variant AND (b) notify all stakeholders.
- Pause and hold if soft thresholds (small regressions) observed — hold for human review.
- Cost throttle: if spend delta crosses threshold, reduce canary slice automatically to safe-tier.

Oncall runbook snippet (operational)
- Triage priority sequence: 1) 5xx/error spike, 2) latency tail, 3) quality regression, 4) cost spike.
- Quick checks: recent deployment rev id, model hash, routing policy version, synthetic probe results.
- Immediate mitigation options: pause canary, route to fallback variant, reduce concurrency, scale more nodes (if dedicated capacity).
- Escalation: if human review required, RS + Model Lead decision within 60 minutes.

Communication templates
- Short incident blurb (for stakeholders): one-sentence summary + immediate action + expected ETA for fix. Example: "Observability: Canary for prompt-routing feature showed p95 latency increase >30% at 09:12. Traffic reduced to fallback model and RS is investigating. Next update in 30m."
- Customer comms (if public): short, supportive, emphasize rollback and customer data safety. Drafts should route through CS liaison.

AB test tie-breaker rules
- If quantitative metrics disagree (product metric improves but quality regresses slightly), defer to quality-first for first 30 days for LLM-visible outputs.
- Define primary metric pre-run and minimum detectable effect; avoid post-hoc metric selection.

Preflight checklist (before T-0)
- [ ] Signal dashboards deployed and validated (links visible)
- [ ] Alerts tested on synthetic breaches
- [ ] Probe dataset uploaded and baseline run complete
- [ ] Rollback policy configured in routing layer
- [ ] Steward, OL, ML, RL and oncall assigned and calendared
- [ ] Comms channel created (Slack + email list) and initial owner pinged
- [ ] Cost guardrails configured and daily budget alarms set

Post-mortem and learnings capture
- Minimum required artifacts after any non-trivial canary: decision log, time-series export, 30-sample blind review, and retrospective notes. Store under: confluence/rollouts/<canary-id>.

Open questions / TODOs (working list)
- How to standardize semantic-score for new languages (Priya to draft cross-lingual rubric).
- Automation: wire up the console to auto-create the Slack channel and add the steward and oncall. (ENG-2389)
- Synthetic probe generation: can we dynamically sample recent production prompts for more realistic probes? (privacy review required).
- Experiment analysis: define template for pre-registered hypotheses and sample size calc.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep canaries small and measurable. If team wants big ramp, require explicit exec signoff.
- Avoid mixing feature toggles and model changes in same canary (separate activations).
- We should add a small library of pre-built probe sets for common domains (search, compose, rerank).

Appendix: quick links and references
- Example alert queries: latency_p95(route="/v1/compose") > baseline*1.3
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-2389 (automation of channels), JIRA-OBS-4021 (dashboard templates)
- Confluence: confluence.redwood/inference/canary-standards (working doc)

If you are the steward: paste this into a new doc and customize baseline numbers for your route. Call out any non-standard exposures (enterprise-only, data-sensitivity) and loop in Security if needed.

-- Ava (draft, 2025-02-03)
